lessons.title: Modal verbs
lessons.summary: können, müssen, dürfen, sollen, wollen, möchten: they say what you can, must, may or want to do, with a second verb at the end.

cards.title: When do you need them?
cards.body: At the doctor's and everywhere else: **Sie müssen viel trinken.** **Ich kann nicht schlafen.** **Darf ich Sport machen?** **Sie sollen drei Tage im Bett bleiben.**

examples.english: I'd like to make an appointment.

cards.title: What each one means
cards.body: **können** = can, be able. **müssen** = must, have to. **dürfen** = may, be allowed. **sollen** = should (someone else says so). **wollen** = want. **möchten** = would like (polite).

examples.english: You're not allowed to work today.

examples.german: Der Arzt sagt, ich **soll** Tabletten nehmen.
examples.english: The doctor says I should take tablets.

cards.title: The bracket again
cards.body: The modal verb is at **position 2**, the second verb goes to the **end** in the infinitive.

cards.title: The forms
cards.body: ich and er/sie/es have **no ending** and are the same. The vowel often changes in the singular.
cards.tip: möchten: ich möchte, du möchtest, er möchte.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'er kannt': **er kann** (no -t). Not 'ich will gehe': the second verb is an **infinitive** at the end. And **ich will** means I want — not 'I will'!

games.prompt: Match the modal and its meaning

pairs.left: The doctor says: take a tablet.
You are allowed to go home.
It's necessary: I have to rest.

games.explanation: sollen = someone tells you; dürfen = permission; können = ability; müssen = necessity.

games.english: You must drink a lot of water.

lessons.title: man
lessons.summary: man means 'one / people in general'. Perfect for rules and advice: Hier darf man nicht rauchen.

cards.title: When do you need it?
cards.body: For rules, instructions and general advice, when it doesn't matter **who** does something: in a hospital, on signs, in health tips. English uses 'you', 'one' or 'people'.

examples.english: You're not allowed to smoke here.

examples.german: Bei Fieber soll **man** im Bett bleiben.
examples.english: With a fever you should stay in bed.

cards.title: Verb like er/sie/es
cards.body: **man** always takes the verb form of **er/sie/es**, even though it means people in general.

examples.english: How do you say that in German?

cards.title: man with modal verbs
cards.body: Very often **man** comes with a modal verb to state rules: **man muss**, **man darf nicht**, **man soll**, **man kann**.

examples.german: In der Apotheke **kann man** Medikamente kaufen.
examples.english: You can buy medicine at the pharmacy.

examples.german: Vor dem Essen **muss man** die Tabletten nehmen.
examples.english: You have to take the tablets before eating.

cards.title: man ≠ Mann
cards.body: **man** (one n, small m) is the pronoun. **der Mann** (two n, capital M) is the man. They sound the same.

examples.english: The man says you have to wait.

cards.tip: man never changes and never refers back: no 'er' for man.

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'man müssen': **man muss**. Not 'Man ist krank, dann er geht zum Arzt': keep **man** — **dann geht man zum Arzt**.

examples.german: Wenn man krank ist, geht **man** zum Arzt.
examples.english: When you're ill, you go to the doctor.

games.english: In hospital you have to be quiet.
games.explanation: man takes the er/sie/es form: muss.
The pronoun is man, the person is der Mann.

games.prompt: Match the sign and its meaning

lessons.title: Imperative
lessons.summary: Telling someone what to do: Komm! Kommt! Kommen Sie! Three forms for du, ihr and Sie.

cards.title: When do you need it?
cards.body: Giving instructions and advice: the doctor (**Nehmen Sie die Tabletten!**), a friend (**Trink viel Tee!**), recipes and signs. With **bitte** it becomes polite.

examples.english: Stay in bed and sleep a lot!

cards.title: Three forms
cards.body: **du**: take the du-form, drop **-st** and the pronoun. **ihr**: the ihr-form without ihr. **Sie**: verb first, **Sie** stays.
cards.tip: du nimmst → Nimm! The e→i change stays, but a→ä disappears: du fährst → Fahr!

cards.title: Separable verbs and sein
cards.body: The prefix goes to the end: **Ruf mich an!** **Steh auf!** And **sein** is irregular: **Sei** ruhig! **Seid** ruhig! **Seien Sie** ruhig!

cards.title: Making it polite
cards.body: Add **bitte** (after the verb or at the start/end) and maybe **doch** or **mal** for friendly advice.

examples.english: Why don't you go to the doctor!

cards.title: Common mistakes
cards.body: Not 'Kommst!' or 'Du komm!': just **Komm!** Not 'Fährst langsam!': **Fahr langsam!** And never drop **Sie**: **Warten Sie!**

games.explanation: Drop -st and du; e→i stays, a→ä goes; sein is irregular.
du: no ending; ihr: -t; Sie: verb + Sie.
